comments.author: @speedomars
comments.text: the biggest hazard is flying in a canyon at high altitude.  there is not enough room to turn. and if your plane is underpowered, you cannot climb out.

replies.author: @Earthcue
replies.text: Wow, so you really have been in that situation. That moment when you realized you couldn't turn must have been intense. Glad you made the right call and got through safely! Thanks for sharing some real flying experience here, this is the kind of insight you don't get from just reading about the Sierras. 🙏🙏🙏

replies.author: @speedomars
replies.text: @Earthcue we are taught about this in training.  also taught about mountain wave winds and how to recognize them (clouds form at the peaks of the wind in tiny groupings at a logarithmic boundaries)..  only once have i been in a situation where i found myself unable to turn as i wanted to, and got dangerously close to terrain (in the Rockies).  i continued to fly straight ahead and lucky did not encounter anything on that flight path until i was able to clear the obstacles and continue on my way.  flying around the Sierras has all these special hazards plus during winter, icing danger.

replies.author: @Earthcue
replies.text: That sounds terrifying, especially when there’s no room left to turn or climb out. You sound like you know flying pretty well. Is this something you’ve experienced yourself?
